idea: Investment committee memo writing for family offices
buyer: Family office principals and single-family CIOs
pain: Decisions made on broker decks; no independent written analysis
v1: One IC memo on a live opportunity
channel: Husband's professional network plus her own
verdict: Good price and genuine retainer potential, but family offices are a segment she reaches by introduction.

why.distribution: 10-20 reachable via husband's network, but each is an introduction rather than a direct relationship.
why.demand: Family offices do pay for outsourced analysis; nothing tested here.
why.fmf: Decision-grade written analysis on unfamiliar assets is the core of her trained skill.
why.revenue_structure: Monthly retainers are normal in this segment and renew by habit.
why.defensibility: Trust-based and sticky once inside, hard to displace but also hard to enter.
why.leverage: Her judgement is the product; templates help only at the margin.
why.time_to_revenue: Introductions then a trial memo: 1-3 months.
why.tailwind: Family office formation is genuinely growing, though slowly and without a budget line.
why.ceiling: £4k/mo x 5 retained offices = £240k, but five retained family offices in year one is the stretch case.

ceiling_arithmetic: £4k/mo x 5 family offices = £240k/yr. Five retainers clears the bar, but each takes months of trust-building; 2 in year one = £96k is the honest expectation.
carries: High price per client, real retainer economics, and only a handful of clients needed.
kills: Access. Family offices are reached one introduction at a time and buy on trust built over quarters.
test: Ask her husband for three named introductions and offer one free IC memo.
test_pass: One asks what a monthly arrangement would cost.
test_fail: Polite interest, no live decision to apply it to.
